subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmeai.com>, Jenna Li <jenna@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models

Hi Samir / Jenna —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Wanted to capture a quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned. Appreciate you walking through Acme AI’s goals and constraints.

High-level pain and goals (what I heard):
- Cost predictability: heavy spend on OpenAI and Anthropic for both completions and embeddings; looking to reduce per-token unit economics.
- Vendor diversification / risk reduction: security/compliance team wants the option to self-host or run in VPC for regulated customers.
- Performance parity & compatibility: existing prompts, function/tooling, and streaming behavior should work with minimal app changes.
- Service-level needs: target 99.9% availability and steady latency for user-facing flows.

Current stack and usage notes you shared:
- Production: OpenAI Chat API (gpt-4.1-style) for chat features; Anthropic for safety-review steps.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings for search + recall.
- Volume: ~12M tokens/month across prod + staging; peak concurrent chat sessions ~400.
- Important integrations: prompt templating with tool-calling (webhook-based actions), streaming responses to clients, and shared tracing/logging in Datadog.

Compatibility & technical requirements you flagged:
- Must support OpenAI / Anthropic API parity for chat + streaming + function/tool calling or provide a compatibility proxy.
- Embedding dimension parity or mapping (we discussed vector transform option).
- KV cache support and low-latency generation for <500ms tail on short prompts.
- SOC2 and audit log evidence required before POC for certain enterprise customers.

Model shortlist we discussed as candidate targets for migration:
- Open models: Redmond-3.1 (4k/16k variants) for chat, Falcon-180B-quant for cost-sensitive throughput, LlamaX-2-13B-quant for embeddings/batched inference.
- Fallbacks: continue Anthropic/OpenAI for a phased rollout where we proxy traffic until parity verified.

Success criteria for a POC / pilot (what success looks like):
1) Feature parity: chat+tool-calling + streaming without user-visible regressions on top 10 prompts.
2) Cost: >=40% reduction in per-token inference cost at pilot throughput.
3) Latency & reliability: 95th percentile latency within 20% of current production for pilot routes and no functional regressions.
4) Compliance: delivery of SOC2 summary + audit log access for the pilot environment.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Technical workshop (1.5 hours) with Eng + Infra (Redwood) and your Platform/SRE to map integration points and traffic samples — proposed week of Nov 8.
- Share a sanitized traffic sample (10-20 representative sessions) and a short list of top 10 prompts we should validate.
- Redwood to provide: SOC2 summary, sample MSA with recommended redlines, and a quick cost/throughput estimate for a dedicated pilot cluster.

Attachments I’ll share with the team: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, Sample_MSA_redlines.docx, technical-workshop-agenda.pdf (attached).

Would you be available for the technical workshop on Tue Nov 10 or Thu Nov 12 (we can shift based on your schedule)? Also, please confirm who from your engineering/security team should join.

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com

>
> Samir

From: Samir Patel <samir@acmeai.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models

Appreciate the recap, Aditya — all that matches what we discussed. A couple clarifications: 
- Embedding parity: our search index relies on 1536-d OpenAI embeddings today; would prefer not to reindex if possible. Can Redwood map/embed to the same dimensionality or offer a mapping strategy?
- Timeline: we need a vendor decision before Jan 15 to include in next quarter budgeting.

We can do Tue Nov 10 at 10:00am PT for the technical workshop — I’ll invite Platform/SRE and a product manager. Please send the agenda and any prep items.

Thanks,
Samir

Samir Patel

samir@acmeai.com

Quick internal note — thanks for the detailed recap. Please be sure to include the following in the workshop packet:
- SOC2 artifact plus a single bullet on audit log retention and access paths (security will want details).
- A short technical note on embedding mapping strategies (dimensionality conversion, projection matrices, or hybrid reindex plan).
- Cost model: sample per-token numbers at pilot and at projected 3x scale for the three shortlisted model variants.
- Can we propose a minimal pilot scope (one chat route + embeddings-backed search) to limit risk?

I’ll coordinate the MSA and point Marissa Legal to the sample redlines. Rishi — can you prepare a short ops-runbook for pilot cluster requirements?

-Marissa

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models

Thanks Samir — confirmed Tue Nov 10 at 10:00am PT. Agenda and prep packet attached (technical-workshop-agenda.pdf).

Addressing two quick items you raised:
- Embedding parity: Redwood supports an embedding-compat layer — we can produce 1536-d vectors via a projection layer on top of our 2k/4k models or run a dedicated small embedding model with the same dim. We’ll include a short benchmark (quality vs reindex cost) in the packet.
- SOC2 evidence: attaching Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf. For the pilot we can provide scoped audit log access (read-only) and an agreed retention window.

Proposed minimal pilot scope:
- One chat route (user-facing conversation path) + embeddings-backed semantic search for product catalog; traffic throttled to pilot throughput (configurable).
- Duration: 4 weeks with defined validation prompts and metrics collection.

Next actions:
1) Acme: share the 10 representative prompts and one sanitized traffic sample by Nov 5.
2) Redwood: provide a short cost estimate and pilot cluster sizing by Nov 7 (I’ll send with Rishi).
3) Legal: once Acme confirms, exchange sample MSA and redlines for review.
\If that looks good I’ll calendar the workshop and loop in our SRE/ops folks.
\Best,
